- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.5), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for volatility.
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above peak for next 3–5 days.
- Model consistently underestimates mean-reversion periods; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast if 3+ consecutive days show price consolidation or downward trend.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to be 1–2% too low in early periods; adjust upward by 1–2% if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model fails to capture momentum shifts; apply smoothing filter to sentiment-weighted average before forecasting.
